subject.title: Improve read tool handling for binary document formats (.docx, .pdf, .pptx, .xlsx) & Avoid Token Waste on Binary Read

question: Should OpenClaw's core read tool add a narrow safe fallback for known binary document formats, or should this remain only in dedicated document/PDF tools?
rationale: Current source confirms the problem, but the durable product choice is whether read should fail helpfully for binary documents or attempt parsing/extraction inline.

options.title: Add narrow read fallback
options.body: Port or review the linked guard so read returns an actionable message for known binary Office/PDF formats and leaves parsing to dedicated tools.

options.title: Defer to document tools only
options.body: Keep read as a text/image tool and rely on docs/tool descriptions plus the pdf/document plugin path for parsing, accepting continued raw binary risk unless descriptions change.

options.title: Expand native parsing
options.body: Treat this as part of broader document ingestion work with security and dependency review across related attachment/file issues.

recommendation.title: Add narrow read fallback
recommendation.body: Port or review the linked guard so read returns an actionable message for known binary Office/PDF formats and leaves parsing to dedicated tools.

likelyOwner.reason: Most relevant available routing signal from recent read-wrapper and release-snapshot history.
